tldr: Headlines across 21 buckets lead overwhelmingly with a single image: Houthi missiles killing three at Riyadh airport, with Ethiopian drone strikes on Eritrean forces as a secondary thread. The Syria coalition-expansion story — which body text marks as the week's most significant development — appears in only four headline slots, meaning readers who scan titles see a story of casualties and strikes rather than a coalition potentially widening by 20,000 Syrian troops.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to frame the Houthi campaign as deliberate isolation strategy — 'cut kingdom off from rest of world' — connecting military action to economic consequences for South Asian diaspora and aviation links.

Only headline to invoke explicit regional conflagration language ('set the whole region ablaze'); exclusive-vocab data confirms 'ablaze' and 'whole' appear only in this bucket, signaling uniquely alarmist regional framing absent from all wire and broadcast headlines.

Only headline to frame the escalation from Tehran's internal perspective ('Tehran sees the gap narrowing'); this diplomacy-to-war threshold angle is invisible in all other 35 outlet headlines, creating a significant headline-body divergence for this outlet.

bottom_line: Headline coverage distills a three-front Red Sea escalation — Houthi airport strikes, Ethiopian-Eritrean border war, Syria's troop-deployment deliberations — to a single dominant image of Houthi missiles killing three at Riyadh airport, leaving the coalition-widening story almost entirely beneath the scroll line.
